checks: Finite inner nets at all sites give polytopal inner fibers. Their placed hull has fibers between the inner approximants and the original fibers by compatibility, so all remain positive for sufficiently small error and converge in Hausdorff distance. The fixed-base marked estimate and feasible mark matching give convergence of maxima and preserve strict badness.

Full-dimensional positive fibers give every continuous direction, and their placements span aff(B), so the placed hull is full-dimensional in the relative product. A facet with zero continuous normal is satisfied throughout every sampled fiber plane and may be omitted. The remaining shared normals are nonzero, with finitely many inequalities and at least one because each fiber is bounded and d≥1.

In a Hausdorff-convergent sequence of positive fibers, boundedness of the family and nonemptiness give a common ball and a lower bound −R on all thresholds after unit normalization. Unit-sphere compactness leaves unit normals in the limit, including if some original unnormalized normals tend to zero. Every sitewise limiting threshold is finite or +∞.

The finite limiting inequalities describe each limit fiber on the whole continuous space. The inclusion from the fiber follows by point approximation. For the reverse, mix any point satisfying the finite inequalities with a limit interior point whose smaller ball persists in late fibers. All finite constraints become strict and the +∞ constraints eventually hold. Passing to the limit and then removing the mixture proves the reverse inclusion.

For each row the limit data on its finite index set F lie in the finite-dimensional restriction of the affine evaluation space. A fixed linear right inverse supplies a correction tending to zero. At all other sites the corrected entries still diverge to +∞ and can be chosen above the corresponding support values. If F is empty the correction is zero and this entire row is redundant. Thus neither divergent thresholds nor vanishing unnormalized normals require increasing N.

A minimizing sequence for the restricted value has a tail in the strict original-depth sublevel, regardless of whether the restricted value equals the unrestricted one. Mass normalization and each affine shear keep the same number of inequalities with nonzero continuous normals, and preserve depth. The all-positive limit from the compactness theorem remains in the class by closure.

Finite sitewise interior balls have strict margins in all nonzero inequalities. The continuous normals have a uniform strictly positive maximum dot product in each unit direction, by the recession-cone criterion and compactness of the sphere. Both margins persist under small coefficient perturbations, proving positivity and boundedness. Affine thresholds preserve every anchored convex combination, so compatibility is automatic for the perturbed rows.

overlap.comparison: This fact proves affine threshold compactification for one moving halfspace on a fixed ball. The present theorem adds the exact global intersection of N rows at positive Hausdorff limits, closure of the shared class under coefficient perturbations in the stated sense, and attainment of its original-depth infimum.

This supplies marked continuity in the approximation step, with maximum convergence obtained by choosing and matching maximizing marks. It does not give a finite shared inequality class or its extremum.

initial_review.readability: The count N refers to a single list representing the sampled fibers. Base-only facets of the placed hull drop from that list, and redundant rows are allowed. The closure conclusion concerns all-positive limits.
initial_review.summary: A strict polytopal approximation gives a finite shared inequality count. Fixed-count closure at positive limits and the original-depth compactness theorem then attain a separate restricted minimum.
